moTa: From the 1st to the 5th of the fifth lunar month, An Nhiên Pagoda celebrates Tết Đoan Ngọ, a mid-year festival that folk tradition calls "bug-killing day." Here, it's a reminder for every family to look after their health as summer arrives: eat fruit, drink enough water, rest, stay cool, and be together. The pagoda garden sets out lychees, plums, watermelon, and leaf-wrapped ash rice cakes.

loiChao.noiDung: Tết Đoan Ngọ is here. The pagoda garden is full of ripe fruit; come pick some.
An Nhiên Pagoda wishes you a healthy, refreshing Mid-Year Festival.
The fifth-month sun is fierce. Come rest in the shade of the pagoda porch.
Hello at the year's midpoint! Remember to drink an extra glass of water today.
Baskets of lychees, plums and watermelon are ready. Stop by for your share.
Happy Đoan Ngọ! May you and your family stay healthy and joyful.
A southern breeze blows across the yard. Sit down and let your shoulders relax.
The kitchen just wrapped a batch of ash rice cakes. Come taste one.
Half the year has passed. Hello, let's take a little rest today.
The lotus pond is in summer bloom. Come out to the porch for the breeze.
The 5th of the fifth month is near. Have you checked on your family today?
The sun is lovely but harsh. Wishing you enough water, rest, and joy today.

thongDiep.noiDung: Mid-year is a good time to check in with your body: Have you slept, eaten, and rested enough?
A plate of summer fruit on the table is a gentle reminder that nature always has gifts for those who slow down.
Hot weather can make tempers flare. When you feel irritated, sip some cool water and breathe slowly.
Many families now take the folk name "bug-killing day" as a reminder to look after their health mid-year.
Resting isn't laziness. It's how you carry on through the second half of the year without burning out.
A Đoan Ngọ breakfast with the whole family can be worth more than any fancy dish.
Avoid the midday sun if you can. Caring for your body is a way of thanking yourself.
Call your grandparents or parents and ask if the heat is wearing them out. A short call, a lasting warmth.
Eating seasonal fruit is living in tune with nature. Each season brings its own fruit, delicious and wholesome.
Half the year is behind you. You don't need to finish every plan, only to know you're heading the right way.
A short afternoon nap can make the rest of your day much easier.
Ash rice cakes are translucent and cool. Some simple gifts take patient work, bit by bit.
In the heat, look out for people working outdoors. Handing someone a cold bottle of water is a simple, everyday kindness.
Your body usually speaks up before it's exhausted. Notice small signals like thirst, fatigue or headaches; if they persist, see a doctor.
Keep the body cool, keep the heart cool. Skipping one argument also helps cool a summer day.
Đoan Ngọ is a time for children and grandchildren to come home. Sharing a single meal is enough to make it a festival.
Swap sugary drinks for water or cool tea. A small habit with lasting benefits.
Try getting up a bit earlier to exercise while it's still cool. Summer mornings are a pleasure.
Customs differ from region to region, but all share the hope that families stay healthy and together.
Don't wait until you're sick to think about your health. A little care each day, and your body will thank you.
A peeled lychee, a slice of red watermelon. Mid-year joy can be that simple.
If you work at a computer all day, stand up every hour, stretch and look into the distance.
Young children and older people tire easily in muggy weather. Keep a closer eye on them these days.
Share a basket of fruit with your neighbors. Neighborly bonds grow from small gifts.
At mid-year, give yourself credit for all the effort that carried you through six months.
Shade is a gift from someone who planted a tree years ago. Today you can plant one for those who come after.
Eat slowly, chew well, don't overeat. Eating in moderation keeps both body and mind light.
Summer can make us rush. Slow down by one beat, and you'll feel the day stretch a little longer.
Resting at the right time helps you work better. Don't hesitate to give yourself a leisurely afternoon.
When the 5th passes, the fruit baskets will empty. Keep drinking enough water and sleeping well all summer.

loiNguyen.noiDung: I vow to take better care of my health in the second half of this year.
May my whole family stay healthy through the hot summer days.
I vow to drink enough water each day and go to bed before midnight.
May my grandparents and parents eat well and sleep soundly this summer.
I vow to be less hot-tempered in the heat, and to speak more slowly and softly.
May those who work out in the sun always have shade and water.
I vow to set aside a whole half-day just to visit my family.
May children have a safe, healthy and playful summer.
I vow to eat more vegetables and fruit, and fewer sweets and fried foods.
May those who are ill recover soon and be cared for by loved ones.
I vow to move my body for at least fifteen minutes each day.
Thank you to the farmers whose hands grew this sweet fruit.
I vow to let myself rest without feeling guilty.
May every family share a warm Đoan Ngọ breakfast together.
I vow to look back on the past six months and adjust my plans to what I can manage.
May drought-stricken areas soon have rain and clean water.
I vow to call a relative far away and ask how they're doing.
May older people living alone have neighbors who stop by.
I vow to keep a cool heart and not let anger last past the day.
May health workers have the strength to care for their patients.
I vow to add a green potted plant to cool a corner of my home.
May all creatures find shade and water through the summer.
I vow to take a short nap instead of forcing myself to work when tired.
May my brothers and sisters always get along and care for each other.
I vow to share good fruit with my neighbors and friends.
May students have a full and rewarding summer break.
I vow to turn off screens earlier so my eyes and mind can rest.
May everyone learn to listen to their body before overdoing it.
I vow to make the rest of this year slower, healthier, and happier.
May the world have more trees and more shade for everyone.

nhiemVu.phanThuong: A jar of cool water under a tree

nhiemVu.moTa: Message a relative or friend to ask how they're doing, and remind them to drink water and rest.

tho: In the fifth month the garden's ripe and sweet
With lychees, plums, and melons green to eat
We gather on the daybed, speaking low
And ask how each is keeping; glad words flow
queDacBiet.loiGiai: Seasonal fruit is the gift of months of tending. This verse reminds you that mid-year joy needs nothing elaborate: a basket of fruit, a bamboo daybed, a few loved ones sitting side by side. When you ask after each other's health, every conversation grows warm. It's a time to renew family bonds after a busy half year for everyone.
queDacBiet.loiKhuyen: This week, invite a loved one to share a plate of fruit and ask each other one honest question: how have you really been?

tho: The summer noon pours sunlight hot and bright
I sip cool water, resting soft and light
I slow my hands, I slow my steps, at ease
The body calm, the heart's small worries cease
queDacBiet.loiGiai: The blazing midday sun is nature's reminder that everything needs a time to rest. This verse advises you not to race against the heat or against your work. Drink a glass of water, sit in the shade, slow down by one beat. When your body is cared for, your mind softens too, and small worries naturally fade.
queDacBiet.loiKhuyen: Today, set a reminder to drink water every two hours and give yourself ten minutes to rest somewhere cool and airy.

queDacBiet.tieuDe: Ash Rice Cakes in Green Leaves
tho: A family wraps rice cakes in leaves, and soon
Their scent of ash and rice fills the afternoon
Together at one loving meal we stay
And count the warmth the half-year brought our way
queDacBiet.loiGiai: Making ash rice cakes takes patience: soaking the rice, wrapping the leaves, cooking for a long time. This verse is about good things made through slow, careful attention, like the bonds within a family. Mid-year is a time to sit together, look at the months behind you and notice how much warmth you've had. If you treasure it, the rest of the year will feel lighter.
queDacBiet.loiKhuyen: Tell a loved one about a happy memory from the past six months, then ask them about theirs.
